idea: Why to-do lists make you less productive
text:
What if writing every task makes you slower? [pause] , I see it all the time: the list grows and the mind gets stuck. Here's the thing: it changes how you think about work. [look at camera]

First, you start counting every small step: [emphasize] one more thing. Then, the brain treats each item like a separate job: [pause], no flow. Next, you check them off too fast: [look down then up]. Finally, the list becomes a barrier: [gesture to chest], not a guide.

The real cost is mental clutter: [soft tone], the task itself loses meaning. Just let the moment breathe.
title: Why to-do lists hurt your focus
